extracted.intended_audience: poets, guest editors, series editors, and contributors concerned with The Best American Poetry selections
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection standards for choosing 75 poems annually for The Best American Poetry series, covering eligibility, process, and aesthetic criteria prioritized by the series and guest editors. Useful for poets submitting work and editors curating volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — reflect diversity and honor excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: "To see whether a single annual volume can accurately reflect the diversity of American poetry and honor excellence regardless of what form it takes, or what idiom it favors, or from which region of the country it comes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The anthology's overarching goal is both representational (diversity of American poetry across forms, idioms, and regions) and evaluative (recognize excellent work). This frames selection choices rather than prescribing a strict aesthetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of poems per volume
rubrics_metrics.description: 75 poems per year selected from the year's literary journals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixed-size anthology: the guest editor selects 75 poems for each annual volume; selection must fit within that limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest editor selection model
rubrics_metrics.description: Different guest editor every year (Pulitzer-winning poets, MacArthur fellows, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rotating guest editor brings a distinct vision annually; the guest editor's taste largely determines which poems constitute 'excellence' in that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series editor long-list curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Lehman as series editor curates a long list; guest editor selects 75
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The series editor ensures continuity and breadth by preparing a long list drawn from journals; the guest editor then exercises final curatorial choice from that pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit per poet
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 3 poems per individual poet
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps how many poems by the same poet may appear in a single volume, preserving diversity of contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author notes included
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets write brief author notes about the poem (form, occasion, method) — included in volume
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected poems are accompanied by short notes from authors explaining form or context, which can inform readers and editors about method or intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-agnostic eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Form-agnostic — sonnet, free verse, prose poem, experimental all eligible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No formal restrictions: traditional and experimental forms are equally considered; judges should evaluate quality across varied formal choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region-agnostic representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Region-agnostic — represents geographic diversity of US
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection aims to include poets from across the United States rather than concentrating on a single region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idiom-agnostic openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Idiom-agnostic — formal/lyric, slam-influenced, flarf, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different poetic idioms and subcultures are accepted; aesthetic plurality is a positive principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence (editorial discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellence — undefined, intentionally; left to guest editor's vision
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No formalized metric for 'excellence' is provided; the concept is deliberately open-ended so the guest editor's judgment determines quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality — fresh angle on language/form
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for work that presents a new or distinct approach to language, subject, or form; novelty in perspective or technique is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound and rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound and rhythm mattering at the line level
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention to sonic qualities, prosody, and line-level musicality is an explicit aesthetic criterion for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive authorial voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorial voice distinctive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poems demonstrating a unique or clear voice are more likely to be recognized; voice helps distinguish work in a crowded field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Magazine publication during the eligibility year
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only poems first published in eligible magazines within the specified year are considered; timing of journal publication determines eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Both large-circulation and small-press journals (and rarely books) are eligible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wide range of publication venues are acceptable, from prominent magazines to small presses, to ensure breadth of discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency / national identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets resident in U.S. (foreign-born OK if community-identified American)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is focused on poets who are part of the American poetic community; birthplace is not determinative if the poet is identified with U.S. literary life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations and non-English works excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Not Eligible: Translations; works in languages other than English (apart from translations of foreign poetry)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only original English-language poems are considered; translated work is generally excluded from selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-book publication exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Not Eligible: Previously published in book before journal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a poem appeared first in a book prior to journal publication, it is not eligible for inclusion; priority of publication matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and range over consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Range and diversity prized over consensus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The series values showcasing a wide spectrum of styles and voices rather than producing a volume that reflects a single critical consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of principles beyond poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles port to short prose: form-agnostic, idiom-agnostic, excellence recognized by practitioners, range and diversity prized
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial principles used for Best American Poetry can inform selection and evaluation in short prose genres: prioritize diversity of form/idiom and rely on practitioner judgment for 'excellence.'
